# The cffdrs oracle fixture

`cffdrs.json` is a sweep of 23,748 FBP cases and what the reference
implementation produces for each. Every `TestCFFDRS*` in the package asserts
against it. It is not in this repository, and it is not supposed to be.

## Why it is not committed

The fixture is 11.7 MB of numbers produced by running
[cffdrs](https://cran.r-project.org/package=cffdrs), the Canadian Forest
Service's own R implementation of the FBP System. cffdrs is **GPL-2**. This
repository is MIT.

Rather than redistribute a bulk artefact generated by GPL software from an MIT
repo, this ships the generator — `gen_cffdrs_reference.R`, its `Dockerfile` and
the `regen-cffdrs.sh` wrapper — and leaves the generating to you. Running cffdrs
locally to produce a test fixture is an ordinary use of it under its own licence,
and imposes nothing on this repository or on anything importing it.

## How to generate it

```
./testdata/regen-cffdrs.sh
```

Docker and nothing else. The container pins R 4.6.1 and cffdrs 1.9.2, so you do
not need R, GDAL, GEOS or PROJ on the host. `--local` uses an `Rscript` already
on `PATH` that has cffdrs installed; `--help` explains the rest.

The first build pulls an R toolchain and GDAL and is slow — ten minutes or so.
After that it is cached and a regeneration takes about half a minute. The sweep
itself is not the slow part.

The known-good fixture, as generated by the pinned versions above and as the
figures in the top-level README were measured against, is:

```
sha256  e0e51ff105f3d029b5ed9f291a7ae2dad59c2f31e0f82e77534efb61d07db8cc
```

Earlier digests are kept so a stale local fixture identifies itself instead of
failing obscurely. Newest first:

| sha256 | cases | recorded before |
|---|---|---|
| `148a5a9e…24cf8f` | 23532 | the FMC sweep block (`foliar.go`), which added the `long`, `elv` and `d0` input columns and 216 rows reaching the elevation branch of eqs. 3/4, the caller-supplied-`D0` branch and six more longitudes. It has none of those three columns, so `TestCFFDRSFoliarMoistureContentReachesEveryBranch` fails on it rather than skipping |
| `12b9a009…89a7f` | 20716 | the M3/M4 mixedwoods (`8b0cf01`), which took `PDF_VALUES` from three values to five, split the M1/M2 and M3/M4 sweeps because they take different blend inputs, and added M3/M4 to the slope block. It has no `M3` or `M4` rows at all, so `TestCFFDRSSlopeBackSolve` logs loudly rather than asserting the eq. 42b/42c readings |
| `612ef152…21058` | ~11500 | the crown-fire sweep, so it carries no `cbh`, `cfl`, `fmc`, `sfc`, `csi` or `rso` columns |

**The move from `148a5a9e` to `e0e51ff1` moved no reference number either.**
`tools/fixture-diff` over the pre-port copy reports *No column shared by both
fixtures moved* across all 23,388 cases the two sweeps share — every one of the
old fixture's rows, with nothing only-in-old. The difference is entirely the 216
added FMC rows and the three input columns they needed. Those columns are why the
digest moved at all: `long`, `elv` and `d0` were constants in the generator until
the FMC block gave them something to say, so every row gained three fields.

**The move from `12b9a009` to `148a5a9e` moved no reference number.** That was
verified rather than assumed, because the digest had simply not been re-recorded
when `8b0cf01` grew the sweep. The pre-M3/M4 generator was checked out and rerun
at these same pins — reproducing `12b9a009` byte for byte, which is what makes
the rest of this trustworthy — and the two fixtures compared with
`tools/fixture-diff`. All fourteen output columns agree across the 18804 cases
the sweeps share. The difference is entirely 4584 added M3/M4 rows and 1800
removed M2 rows that `8b0cf01` identified as duplicates of rows already present.

One property worth knowing: 144 of those cases are emitted twice, because the
slope block repeats the flat block at `gs = 0`. They are exact duplicates in both
inputs and outputs, so they cost a little time and nothing else.

## What happens without it

`go test ./...` passes. Seventeen fixture-backed tests skip with a message pointing
here; everything else — the identities, round-trips, rotational invariance and
NaN sweeps — runs unconditionally, and is what CI checks on every push.

Those unconditional tests forbid most transcription errors. They cannot catch the
one class that matters most: an error inherited from the 1992 source itself,
where a second careful transcription agrees precisely in being wrong. That is
exactly what the grass-curing bug was. Only the oracle finds those, which is why
`.github/workflows/oracle.yml` regenerates this fixture and runs the
`TestCFFDRS*` tests for real, monthly and on demand. Dispatch it after changing a
coefficient — it is not on push, because each run rebuilds the container.

## How to read a regeneration

Both pinned versions are recorded *into* the fixture (`cffdrs_version`,
`r_version` at its top level) and logged by every `TestCFFDRS*`, so a version
drift announces itself rather than silently moving several thousand numbers.

A changed reference number is the oracle telling you something, not noise to be
committed past. Read the diff — with `tools/fixture-diff`, not with your eyes:

```
cp testdata/cffdrs.json /tmp/cffdrs.old.json
./testdata/regen-cffdrs.sh
go run ./tools/fixture-diff /tmp/cffdrs.old.json testdata/cffdrs.json
```

It keys cases by their inputs rather than by row order, so a widened sweep is not
a diff; it reports per column whether anything moved, by how much, and in which
cases; and it exits non-zero when something did. Adding a column to the generator
should print `No column shared by both fixtures moved.` — if it prints anything
else, that is the finding, and it belongs in the PR.
